sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Ryan Bennett. 2018 preprint (2020). Prosody in Mesoamerican languages. In Gussenhoven & Chen (eds.), Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cites Jany 2011 only for syllable structure/phonation; gives stress statements for Ayutla, Tamazulápam, Alotepec Mixe but none for Chuxnabán/Quetzaltepec.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only the ISO row 'Mixe, Quetzaltepec' (pxm); no lect record, no stress coding.

sources.citation: Jany, Carmen. 2011. The Phonetics and Phonology of Chuxnabán Mixe. Linguistic Discovery 9(1): 31-70. doi:10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.388
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: No stress/accent section and no placement rule. Only incidental: vowel measurements taken from 'stressed syllables in monosyllabic words' (p.54); marginal vowels [ae, oe, Y] 'are only found in stressed syllables.. the three vowels simply do not occur in unstressed syllables' (p.58). Transcriptions carry IPA stress marks (e.g. [ˈtsoˀkpɨ] 'to heal') without comment. p.31 establishes identity: Chuxnabán Mixe 'corresponds to Quetzaltepec Mixe in the Ethnologue entry'.

sources.citation: Aguilar Morales, Guadalupe. 2025. Las cláusulas relativas en el mixe de Chuxnabán, Quetzaltepec. Tesis de maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS/INPI, Ciudad de México. 512 pp. Sec. 2.2 'El esbozo fonológico del mixe de Chuxnabán', pp. 21-29.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sketch covers consonants, vowels and nucleus types only; the word 'acento' never occurs; no stress rule. Phonetic forms mark stress (final in disyllables such as [ʔa.ˈbiːts] 'oscuro', [ku.ˈwaːy] 'cabello', [ʔa.ˈduʔuk] 'solo') without comment; p.362 says adnominal demonstratives/determiners are 'sílabas átonas'.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No placement statement; p.26: in Sayula Popoluca obstruent voicing is stress-sensitive, 'this has not been observed for Chuxnabán Mixe'.

sources.citation: Jany, Carmen. 2010. Orthography design for Chuxnabán Mixe. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 231-253. hdl:10125/4481
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No mention of stress/accent; orthography discussion covers vowels, length, laryngeal features, loans, palatalization, word boundaries. p.232 repeats the Quetzaltepec Mixe identity.

sources.citation: Romero-Méndez, Rodrigo. 2008. A Reference Grammar of Ayutla Mixe. PhD, SUNY Buffalo; Santiago Martínez, Godofredo. 2015. Temas de fonología y morfosintaxis del mixe de Tamazulápam. PhD, CIESAS (held under tlah1239).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked only for Quetzaltepec/Chuxnabán mentions: both cite Jany 2006/2011 as the only phonological work on this variety; Santiago Martínez pp.6-7 notes Wichmann 1995 does not cover Quetzaltepec. No stress statement for pxm.

sources.citation: Jany, Carmen. 2007. Phonemic versus phonetic correlates of vowel length in Chuxnabán Mixe. Proceedings of the Berkeley Linguistics Society 33(2). doi:10.3765/bls.v33i2.3502
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement; conclusion lists 'the effects of position in word, stress, and intonation on vowel length' as future work.

sources.citation: Jany, Carmen. 2006 [vol. 2007]. Vowel Length and Phonation Contrasts in Chuxnabán Mixe. Santa Barbara Papers in Linguistics 18 (Proc. 9th WAIL). UCSB.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Chuxnabán stress placement; only reports Hoogshagen 1959 that Coatlán vowel length does not depend on stress.

sources.citation: Jany, Carmen. 2013. Defining Nominal Compounding as a Productive Word-Formation Process in Chuxnabán Mixe. International Journal of American Linguistics 79(4): 533-553.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Abstract states Chuxnabán compounds 'are best discerned phonologically'; the phonological criterion is very likely word stress (one primary stress per compound), so the paper probably states where primary stress falls in simple and compound nouns -- the only Jany publication likely to contain an explicit stress rule for pxm.
